{•}ByteQuest.

Your progress belongs to you.

Last updated November 14, 2026

What the app stores

When you practise as a guest, ByteQuest saves drafts, notes, problem completion, review dates, confidence ratings and practice history in your browser. If you sign in, Firebase Authentication manages your Google account’s basic profile and email for identity, and ByteQuest saves your learning progress in the project’s Supabase database. The backend also stores your Firebase account identifier, verified email, account creation date and most recent account request date.

Who can see it

Published problems and their practice tests are public. Drafts, notes and learning progress are scoped to your signed-in user account through a backend that verifies Firebase tokens and selects only that account’s records. Browser clients cannot directly read the private account tables. The project owner can administer the database and Firebase authentication accounts. Unpublished problems and private test suites are available to their authors and appointed library editors. Every verified signed-in learner can create problems; only the author or an editor can change an existing problem.

Where code runs

Your Java solution compiles and executes on your device through CheerpJ. Signed-in drafts can be saved as part of your progress. Practice test results and points are personal learning records, rather than independently verified competition scores.

Online status

If enabled on your discoverable profile, online status uses short-lived page sessions and a 30-second activity timeout. Only activity timing is sent; cursor positions and typed content are not collected. Hidden, unfocused and closing pages send an offline update. If the browser cannot deliver it, the session expires within 30 seconds of its last activity.

Online code execution

C, C++ and Python runs send your source code and public or custom practice inputs through our authenticated API to the Wandbox sandbox. ByteQuest requests no public permalink. Account tokens, email addresses, private notes and private hidden test suites are not sent to Wandbox. The online service has execution and fair-use limits.

Services the app uses

GitHub Pages hosts the website. Firebase Authentication manages Google sign-in and the browser session. Supabase provides the database and the account API. The browser also loads the Java runtime from CheerpJ, the Firebase SDK from Google’s CDN, and fonts from Google Fonts. These services receive the network request information needed to provide their features.

Backups and signing out

Use Backup to export your progress without authentication tokens. Sign out ends this app’s session on the current device and keeps the account’s saved progress. Guest work is kept separate from account work unless you choose to import it. Clearing browser site data removes local copies and sign-in state; it does not delete cloud records.

Deleting your account

Choose Delete account from the account menu or Edit profile. Type DELETE and verify your Google identity. ByteQuest removes your profile, learning progress, notes, drafts, uploaded photo, follows, roles and unpublished authored problems. Published problems and their tests stay in the community library without your account attribution. Your Firebase sign-in for this app is deleted; your Google account is kept.

A private hashed account marker prevents an old sign-in token from restoring removed records and tracks retryable cleanup. The current browser clears this account’s cached learning data. Local copies on other devices can be cleared in those browsers. Export a backup before deleting if you want to keep your own copy.

Project owner

ByteQuest is maintained through its GitHub repository. Contact the project owner about access or account-removal issues. Avoid posting private information in public issues.

Your optional community profile

You choose your username, display name, bio, optional HTTPS image URL and whether your profile is discoverable. Other signed-in learners can search discoverable profiles, view their activity days and self-reported solved count, points and global rank, and see public follow relationships. Emails, Firebase account IDs, drafts and notes are not included. Turn discoverability off in Edit profile to hide your profile from others; existing follow records are retained but hidden.

Profile images load from the HTTPS host you choose. That host can receive normal image requests. Leave the image empty to use initials. ByteQuest does not automatically publish your Google photo or name.

Creators and your inbox

Library administrators can grant creators access to author, correct and publish problems and view private tests. New published problems and corrections appear in every signed-in learner’s in-app inbox. Notifications are fetched when the inbox opens or regains focus, not sent by email or push. Your read status is stored privately.

Private tests

Private cases stay on the backend. If a trusted server judge is configured, submitting a private-suite solution sends your code and the private inputs to that judge for isolated Java execution. The learner receives an aggregate verdict, without hidden inputs or outputs. Private judging is not activated in this release; public practice runs locally.

Device photo uploads and comparisons

You can choose a JPG, PNG or WebP photo. ByteQuest crops and re-encodes it as a small JPEG, removing original metadata, and stores it in private Supabase Storage. Profile image links expire after ten minutes; previously issued links can stay usable until expiry after you hide a profile. Discoverable profiles share valid UTC solve dates and topics for activity comparisons with multiple followed friends, alongside existing practice totals. Code and notes stay private.

Light/dark preference is stored on your device. Python, C and C++ public practice runs use the authenticated Wandbox compiler service described above. Private hidden-test execution remains a separate server feature.
